subject: ChatGPT writes RTL 🧠, Google books rocket launch 🚀, California subpoenas Nvidia ⚖️
notes: No funding rounds, acquisitions, IPOs, funds or model pricing in this issue; only top news stories extracted. AMD/Unsloth sponsor block ignored.

stories.headline: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over whether chips or confidential information reached China
stories.quote: AG Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena asking whether Nvidia's chips or confidential data ended up in China, and whether Nvidia misled investors about that risk under California securities law.

facts.text: The probe follows Jensen Huang's resignation and centers on Megaspeed, a Singapore data center operator suspected of diverting restricted chips, and on how Nvidia reports overseas revenue.
facts.quote: The probe follows Jensen Huang's resignation and centers on Megaspeed, the Singapore data center operator suspected of diverting restricted chips, plus how Nvidia reports overseas revenue.

facts.text: Nvidia's market value has dropped over $1 trillion in two weeks; Nvidia has not commented.
facts.quote: Nvidia's market value has dropped over $1 trillion in two weeks, and it hasn't commented yet.

stories.headline: OpenAI's models rewrote RTL for AMD GPU IP with up to 14% PPA gains and 10% to 13% smaller blocks on OpenAI's Jalapeño chip
stories.quote: The models rewrote SystemVerilog for AMD's already-optimized GPU blocks, with some changes in a design sent for manufacturing and single-digit gains verified on its next flagship CPU.

facts.text: On Jalapeño, the matrix and SIMD blocks shrank 10% to 13%, confirmed in silicon.
facts.quote: On Jalapeño, the matrix and SIMD blocks shrank 10% to 13%, confirmed in silicon, partly by rewriting adders and multipliers, including a multiplier cut from two cycles to one.

facts.text: OpenAI is training GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys to drive EDA tools directly.
facts.quote: OpenAI is also training GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys to drive EDA tools directly.

stories.headline: Google books a dedicated New Glenn launch in Q1 2029 for Project Suncatcher, its orbital TPU compute constellation
stories.quote: The mission is Google's first dedicated heavy-lift launch for the project, using New Glenn's large payload volume. The booking is for 2029 even though New Glenn's hotfire anomaly investigation is still ongoing.

facts.text: Each Suncatcher satellite carries roughly a data center rack's worth of computing, solar powered in sun-synchronous orbit.
facts.quote: Each Suncatcher satellite carries roughly a data center rack's worth of computing and runs on solar power in sun-synchronous orbit, forming an interconnected network of TPUs for machine learning compute.

stories.headline: Meta reportedly prices its pocket-sized Muse Charm at $300 with a free year of Verizon 5G and delays its smartwatch to 2027
stories.quote: Meta plans a December launch and pushed its smartwatch to 2027 to make room, and it didn't deny the pricing report.

facts.text: Charm has a roughly 2-inch screen and carries the Muse AI agent.
facts.quote: Charm has a roughly 2-inch screen navigated with a thumb and a customizable Muse character at its center, and it carries the Muse AI agent into the real world.

facts.text: Bundled 5G data from Verizon runs up to 12 months.
facts.quote: The bundled 5G data, up to 12 months from Verizon, is meant to speed Muse's responses away from Wi-Fi.

stories.headline: Relativity finishes Terran R second-stage testing and interstage structural qualification; still targets a late 2026 debut
stories.quote: Relativity still targets a late 2026 debut, though observers expect 2027.

facts.text: The second stage hot-fired at NASA Stennis's A2 stand and the interstage passed structural testing in Long Beach.
facts.quote: The second stage hot-fired at NASA Stennis's A2 stand, and the interstage passed structural testing on Long Beach's “Tender Loving Crusher” rig.

stories.headline: IEA says data center electricity use doubles by 2030, with US gas and Chinese coal pushing emissions up 70%
stories.quote: The IEA projects data centers going from about 120 GW today to roughly 1,000 TWh a year by 2030.
